benchmark: LeadLens vs Claude Deep Research vs Claude+Vibe — decision-layer (TEST 1)

customer_context.company: Meridian Transition Partners (ASSUMED-FOR-FIXTURE — no real private facts)
customer_context.type: US specialized B2B consultancy / professional services
customer_context.service: post-merger integration (PMI) operational execution — first-120-day integration of operations, supply chain and ERP after an acquisition
customer_context.constraints: boutique, limited BD capacity; choosing the wrong accounts wastes meaningful commercial time
customer_context.known: the service and the customer's limited BD capacity
customer_context.unknown: everything about the candidate accounts' current state — to be researched by each arm

commercial_objective: Determine which companies in this candidate set deserve our commercial attention now for our post-acquisition integration consulting service, why, what evidence supports that conclusion, and what we should do next.
candidate_universe_selection_method: Neutral rule, fixed BEFORE any arm ran and WITHOUT pre-checking LeadLens evidence: 7 real, publicly-traded US mid-market industrial manufacturers (plausible structural fit for PMI services), explicitly EXCLUDING the accounts LeadLens already researched in development (CECO, Hillman, and the earlier seed set Standex/Kadant/Franklin/Mayville/Enpro/Chart). Variation in M&A cadence was NOT engineered — it emerges from research.
required_output_question: For each company: should the consultancy spend effort now, why/why-now, what evidence supports it, what weakens it, what remains unknown, and what to do next — and which companies deserve attention first.
